bib.title: UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection for Dimension Reduction

question: Can a dimension reduction algorithm built on Riemannian geometry and fuzzy simplicial sets match t-SNE's visualization quality, keep more global structure, run faster, and embed into any dimension?
hypothesis: A topologically grounded k-neighbour graph method (local-connectivity constraint, fuzzy union, cross-entropy layout) gives embeddings comparable to t-SNE locally, better at non-local scales, and much faster scaling.
contributions: A theoretical framework for manifold learning/dimension reduction in terms of fuzzy simplicial sets and Riemannian geometry
A practical scalable algorithm (UMAP) with no computational restriction on embedding dimension
Empirical comparison with t-SNE, LargeVis, Laplacian Eigenmaps, PCA and Isomap on quality, stability and runtime
A reformulation of t-SNE and LargeVis in the same graph-construction plus graph-layout language (Appendix C)

method.summary: UMAP builds a weighted k-nearest-neighbour graph with per-point local-connectivity offset rho_i and bandwidth sigma_i, symmetrises it with the probabilistic t-conorm, initialises with a spectral layout, then minimises edge-wise fuzzy-set cross entropy by SGD with edge sampling and negative sampling. Experiments compare embeddings by kNN-classifier accuracy, Procrustes stability under subsampling, and wall-clock runtime.

models.name: UMAP
models.architecture: k-NN graph + force-directed layout (no neural network)
models.init_from: spectral embedding of the symmetric normalised Laplacian

other.implementation: Python with numba, single core in the experiments

other.n_iter: default 1000, raised to 1500 for flow cytometry stability

other.threads: default 8 threads on the 4-core machine; single thread in Fig 11

training.objective: Minimise fuzzy-set cross entropy C = sum mu log(mu/nu) + (1-mu) log((1-mu)/(1-nu)) between high-dim graph and low-dim graph; only the second sum is optimised
training.optimizer: SGD with probabilistic edge sampling (sample with probability mu) and negative sampling
training.epochs: n-epochs is a hyper-parameter; value used in experiments not stated
training.hardware: Table 3: MacBook Pro 3.1 GHz Intel Core i7, 8GB RAM; large-scale runs: server with Intel Xeon E5-2697v4, 512GB RAM; 30M-integer run: large memory SMP

other.n_neg_samples: named n-neg-samples in Algorithm 5, value not given
other.a_b_fit: non-linear least squares of Phi=(1+a x^{2b})^-1 against Psi (1 if dist<=min-dist else exp(-(dist-min-dist)))
other.complexity: O(kN) optimisation; overall bounded by NN-Descent, empirically ~O(N^1.14)
other.negative_sample_distribution: uniform approximation of the vertex sampling distribution

inference.samples: kNN accuracy: mean (+- as printed) over 10 folds (Pen digits, COIL-20, Shuttle) or 20 folds (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST); number of runs/seeds per embedding not stated

metrics.name: kNN classifier accuracy on the embedding
metrics.definition: accuracy of a k-nearest-neighbour classifier trained on the embedding, cross-validated; k varied from 10 to 160 (small sets) and 100 to 3200 (large sets)

metrics.name: Normalized Procrustes distance
metrics.definition: distance after optimal translation, uniform scaling and rotation between a subsample embedding and the matching subsample of the full-data embedding, after dividing by the average norm of the embedding

eval.protocol: kNN: stratified 10-fold CV (Pen digits, COIL-20), 10-fold CV (Shuttle), 20-fold CV (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST). Stability: flow cytometry subsamples. Runtime: single-core UMAP; parameters of baselines tuned 'where possible'. No significance tests beyond printed +- values.

limits: No ablation of algorithmic components or hyper-parameters (authors list a comprehensive empirical study as future work, Section 7).
Global structure preservation is argued from visual inspection and kNN accuracy at large k; the authors note there are no clear objective measures of global structure (Section 7).
Hyper-parameters (n, min-dist, n-epochs, embedding dimension) used in the quality and runtime experiments are not stated; baselines were tuned 'where possible'.
Authors concede Kobak and Linderman found t-SNE with the same initialisation can match UMAP on a global-structure measure.
UMAP lacks PCA-style interpretability, can find spurious 'constellation' structure in noise, trades metric preservation for topology, and is weaker below ~500 samples.

Runtimes use single-core UMAP against optimised C++ baselines on different machines per experiment; Table 3 mixes subsampled and PCA-reduced datasets; scRNA is 20,921 cells in text but 21086x1000 in Table 3, Flow is 10% of 1M but 100000x17 in Table 3.
Isomap did not finish for datasets larger than COIL-20 and Laplacian Eigenmaps failed on GoogleNews.
No seed counts or repeat runs reported for kNN accuracy; Fashion-MNIST small-k accuracy is worse than t-SNE.
